To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the black hole production in the parameter range considered in the CMS analysis is not described by the semi-classical picture of black hole, but by quantum gravity, (ii) the black holes are not produced at all in the parameter range, and (iii) the result of the CMS analysis is thus not a direct limit on black holes, but on quantum gravity effects.

the black hole search by CMS Collaboration is invalid in the parameter range they consider, because the black hole production cross section in this parameter range is much larger than that predicted by the semi-classical picture, which has been used by CMS Collaboration to interpret the result.

the parameter range used by CMS is out of the validity region of semi-classical gravity and the Monte Carlo simulation used by CMS is based on a model which is not applicable for the parameter range used.
